cim: Holness announces plans to bring artificial intelligence infrastructure to Jamaica
kihagyva: P3: 42 pont, tendencia 20%, jóváhagyás után fordul
cim_eredeti: Holness announces plans to bring artificial intelligence infrastructure to Jamaica
szoveg_eredeti:
The Jamaican government has approved a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a group of investors to explore the establishment of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure on the island, as part of efforts to position the country to benefit from the rapidly expanding technology sector.

Prime Minister Dr. Andrew Holness made the announcement on Sunday, November 15, during the Jamaica Labour Party's (JLP) special delegates conference at the Montego Bay Convention Centre in St. James.

Holness said the initiative is intended to ensure that Jamaica becomes more than a consumer of AI technology and instead plays a role in its development, while creating employment opportunities for future generations.

“...so that Jamaica can have a footprint and not only be a consumer of the technology, but we can be a part of the creation of the technology,” Holness said.

“And that is something that your administration intends to pursue so that your children can have jobs in the new economy that is going to be created using artificial intelligence,” he added.

The prime minister did not identify the investors involved or disclose the financial value of the proposed agreement. He also did not indicate whether the MOU would involve the establishment of AI data centers in Jamaica.

However, he emphasized that the government recognizes the transformative potential of artificial intelligence and is taking steps to ensure that the country can participate in the emerging global industry.

Holness said the government's AI task force is providing advice on the measures Jamaica needs to implement to capitalize on opportunities presented by the technology.

He described artificial intelligence as the next major technological revolution, predicting that it would significantly increase global productivity and reshape economic activity.

“We sit on the cusp of another transition in technology, another revolution in technology that is going to increase the productivity of mankind far beyond what we can even imagine now. And that is called the artificial intelligence revolution,” Holness said.

“My friends, we cannot be left behind again. We cannot be left behind again.”

The announcement signals the government's intention to pursue investment in AI-related infrastructure as part of its broader economic development agenda.

While details of the proposed facilities and investment arrangements have not yet been disclosed, the initiative could create opportunities for Jamaica to participate in AI development and support the growth of technology-related employment.

The government has not announced a timeline for signing the MOU or implementing any projects arising from the proposed agreement.
